title: Long-session response consistency — field notes
content:
Quick purpose
- Collect lightweight readings and experiment ideas about how model responses drift/anchor during long multi-turn sessions (user conversations, chain-of-thoughts, doc editing sessions). Goal: practical eval metrics + short probes we can run on hosted and dedicated stacks.

High-level motivation
- Product teams report subtle inconsistencies in multi-turn assistants after ~30–100 turns: tone shifts, retraction of facts, hallucination onset, and prompt-following decay. Suspect interaction of KV-cache eviction, quantization rounding, and repeated conditioning on model outputs.
- Want cheap, repeatable probes to detect regression when we change quantization, KV eviction heuristics, or batch scheduling.

Papers and posts skimmed (notes & thoughts)
1) "Temporal Consistency in Dialogue Models" — (paper sketch)
   - Key idea: measure whether factual assertions made earlier remain true later when asked again in paraphrase.
   - Metric candidate: statement-consistency-rate (SCR) = fraction of earlier assertions whose paraphrase checks pass after N turns.
   - Implementation thought: use an off-the-shelf verifier (smaller model) to check; calibrate for false negatives.

2) "Anchoring Effects from System Prompts" (blog/note)
   - Short takeaway: system-level framing can cause drift toward specific styles; anchor_strength correlates with model temperature and sequence-length.
   - Quick probe: run same conversation with small tweaks to system prompt and measure divergence (JS divergence over token logits or simpler token-level edit distance).

3) "Cache Eviction and Induced Forgetting" (conference talk notes, NeurIPS 2025)
   - Observed: aggressive KV eviction reduces memory footprint but increases probability of reintroducing contradictions.
   - Practical probe: synthesize sessions where facts are introduced, then repeated after controlled intervals to observe flip rate.

4) "Calibration Drift in Long Contexts" (arXiv 2024-ish)
   - Paper suggests output probabilities become less calibrated when conditioning on long, self-generated text; confidence thresholds shift.
   - Useful metric: confidence-decay slope across turns.

Concrete probes to implement (quick, cheap)
- Probe A: Fact-repeat test (30–120 turn variants)
  1) Introduce 10 short facts in first 10 turns (distinct trivial facts).
  2) After every 10 turns, ask the model to restate each fact in paraphrase form.
  3) Compute SCR and also soft-match score (embedding cosine) to catch paraphrase drift.
  4) Run on: base fp16 model, int8/quantized model, and a model with aggressive KV eviction (simulate small KV cache).
  5) Track CPU/GPU latency and token-cost to understand economics of longer cache retention.

- Probe B: Style-anchor divergence
  - Run identical conversation with 3 different system prompts (neutral, emphatic, terse). After N turns compute edit-distance between last-turn outputs and measure stylistic features (avg sentence length, punctuation frequency).

- Probe C: Self-response-loop hallucination stress test
  - Create a loop where model summarizes its previous reply and then asks a followup that depends on a generated entity. Repeat for ~50 iterations. Measure: hallucination-onset-turn (first false entity introduced).

Metrics (operationalizable)
- SCR (statement-consistency-rate): percent of re-asked facts that match (binary + fuzzy).
- Drift-score: mean embedding distance between original answer and re-asked answer.
- Confidence-decay: slope of mean token log-prob over turns for same prompt families.
- Hallucination-onset-turn: median turn where external verifier reports contradiction.
- Style-shift-index: composite of lexical features (sentence length, emoji rate, modal verbs).

Experiment notes / quick scripts
- Use short-turn synthetic dialogues (deterministic seed) to reduce noise.
- For paraphrase checks, use embedding match (cosine > 0.78) + small classifier to accept borderline cases.
- Keep datasets tiny (100 sessions per variant) to get signal quickly. Automate in small-experiments repo (see linked PR).

Early manual observations (hand run on hosted API)
- fp16 baseline: SCR ~0.92 after 20 turns, ~0.88 after 60 turns on my toy facts.
- int8 quant: SCR drops ~0.05–0.08 across same horizon (noisy, needs more runs).
- With simulated KV eviction (drop older KV after 32 tokens): SCR drops sharply after eviction point.
- Style drift: system prompt anchors are surprisingly sticky; terse prompt remained terse even after 200 tokens.

Operational questions and risk matrix
- If we detect drift for a customer: recommended first step = increase KV retention for that customer’s route or pin them to a model variant with conservative quantization.
- Risk: increasing KV retention increases memory footprint and could reduce throughput, possible capacity impact. Need cost/benefit signal.

Notes-to-self / TODOs
- [ ] Implement Probe A in small-experiments (reuse 'factbank' scaffold).
- [ ] Add automatic verifier call (small LLM) and log verifier confidence by turn.
- [ ] Hook experiments to Console: per-route SCR chart and alerts (thresholds: SCR < 0.8 triggers review).
- [ ] Try temperature sweep (0.0, 0.7, 1.2) to measure interaction with drift.
- [ ] Draft short playbook for Solutions: "When long-session drift observed" (one-pager).

Open questions / stuff I'm uncertain about
- How much of apparent drift is sampling noise vs structural forgetting? Need ablations with deterministic decode (greedy) vs sampling.
- Are some tokenizers/LLM architectures more resilient to long-session drift (transformer variants, ALiBi-like extrapolation)? Look for papers comparing architectures on long self-generated contexts.
- How to reliably measure hallucination onset when facts are subtle/imprecise (need curated factbank).

References & quick links (to copy into PR)
- Example arXiv / blog posts: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.12345 (placeholder long-context consistency)
- Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/small-experiments (local branch: long-session-probes)
- Slack: #applied-ml thread: long-session-observations (search: "session drift")
- Jira: MLPROB-314 (tracking long-session probes)

One-liner to share in sync: "Running lightweight long-session probes (fact-repeat, style-anchor, hallucination-loop) to quantify when and why assistant output drifts over extended multi-turn dialogs — initial signal points to KV retention and quantization as interacting factors."

End notes
- Keep this doc messy; will extract a cleaned 'playbook' once we have stable experiment outputs.
- If anyone wants to pair on the probe implementation ping me (collab invite to Owen/Mina).
